may_be_looking_for: A diagnosis of systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE) according to specific criteria
High disease activity as measured by a SLEDAI-2000 score of 8 or higher
On a stable dose of one or more standard SLE treatments before starting the study
Willing and able to provide written consent and follow the study protocol
may_exclude_people_who: Received rituximab or any B-cell depleting drug within 9 months before the study
Have a CD4+ T lymphocyte count below 200 cells/μL
Received cyclophosphamide within 8 weeks before the study
Received certain other medications like calcineurin inhibitors recently
patient_summary: This study tests a new drug called MIL62 against a placebo to see if it helps people with systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE). The study is currently recruiting participants in China.
patient_title: A Study of MIL62 for Systemic Lupus Erythematosus (SLE)
questions_to_ask_clinician: Does my disease activity meet the required SLEDAI-2000 score?
Have I taken any B-cell depleting drugs like rituximab in the past 9 months?
What is my CD4+ T lymphocyte count?
Do I have sufficient organ function for this study?
Am I on a stable dose of standard SLE treatments?
Have I taken cyclophosphamide or calcineurin inhibitors recently?
uncertainty_notes: This is a Phase 3 clinical trial, meaning the drug is being tested in a larger group of people to confirm its study outcomes and monitor side effects.
Participants will be randomly assigned to receive either MIL62 or a placebo.
The results of this study are not yet known, and there is no guarantee that MIL62 will be associated with the study outcome or safe.
Participation is voluntary, and you can withdraw at any time.
what_researchers_are_studying: Researchers are studying whether MIL62 is associated with the study outcome and safe for treating systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE) compared to a placebo. This is a Phase 3 trial, which is the final stage of testing before potential approval.
